claims.text: The patient presented with three days of productive cough with yellow sputum, subjective fevers, and increasing shortness of breath on exertion, and denied chest pain.
Community-acquired pneumonia of the right lower lobe and hypertension were documented.
The chest X-ray showed right lower lobe consolidation and no pleural effusion.
Initial white blood cell count was 15.2 x10^9/L, C-reactive protein was 142 mg/L, and creatinine was 0.9 mg/dL.
On hospital day 1, the patient was admitted to the medical ward and started intravenous Antibiotic B; blood cultures were drawn before the first dose, and sputum culture was requested.
Supplemental oxygen by nasal cannula was planned to keep saturation above 92%; the night nursing note documented oxygen at 2 L/min with saturation 94%.
Medication A 5 mg daily was ordered for hypertension. The night nursing note documented the first intravenous Antibiotic B dose at 22:15, with no reaction observed.
On hospital day 2, the patient reported less shortness of breath than on admission, with persistent cough and yellow sputum.
On hospital day 2, white blood cell count was 12.1 x10^9/L and C-reactive protein was 96 mg/L; blood cultures showed no growth to date, and sputum culture was pending.
Community-acquired pneumonia was documented as improving on hospital day 2; hypertension was also documented.
Intravenous Antibiotic B was continued, and oxygen was weaned to 1 L/min with further weaning as tolerated planned.
On hospital day 3, white blood cell count was 9.4 x10^9/L and C-reactive protein was 51 mg/L; blood cultures showed no growth to date, and sputum culture showed normal respiratory flora.

On hospital day 3, intravenous Antibiotic B was switched to oral Antibiotic B, and supplemental oxygen was discontinued after hypoxemia was documented as resolved; nursing documented the first oral dose.
The progress note documented room-air oxygen saturation of 96%; nursing documented ambulation of 50 meters without oxygen and saturation of 95% after walking.
Medication A dose documentation on hospital day 3 was conflicting: the progress note documented 10 mg daily, while the nursing note documented Medication A 5 mg given that shift.
On hospital day 4, community-acquired pneumonia was documented as improved, and hypertension was documented.
At discharge, the patient was documented as clinically stable and improved, with mild residual cough and no shortness of breath at rest.
At discharge, blood cultures showed no growth to date with final results pending, and sputum culture showed normal respiratory flora.
The patient was discharged home with a plan to complete oral Antibiotic B for a total of 7 days of antibiotic therapy, and Medication A was continued.
Primary care clinic follow-up in 1 week and repeat chest X-ray in 6 weeks were planned; the primary care clinic was to follow up final blood culture results.
Final blood culture results were pending at discharge.
